q: 1. According to the Civil Service Act 2049, leave is merely; a/an:
explain: The Act explicitly states that leave is a privilege and not a right; the authority can refuse or cancel leave based on the exigency of work.

q: 2. How many types of leave are provided under the Civil Service Act, 2049?
explain: There are 9 types of leave: Casual, Festival, Home, Sick, Maternity/Maternity Care, Study, Extraordinary, Substitution, and Paternity leave.

q: 3. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, there is a provision that employees can get festival leave without increasing it by ------- days throughout the year.
explain: Civil servants are granted 6 days of casual leave and 6 days of festival leave (total 12) per year.

q: 4. What does a suspended employee get during the period of suspension from the regular job, as per to Civil Service Act, 2049?
options: Half of the salary amount and festival allowance
Half of the salary amount and half of the festival allowance
One fourth of the salary amount and festival allowance
explain: During suspension, an employee is only entitled to half of their basic salary to meet subsistence needs.

q: 5. According to Civil Service Rules-2050, how many days civil servant can get sick leave per year?
explain: A civil servant is entitled to 12 days of fully paid sick leave every year.

q: 6. For the appointment of which position parliamentary hearing process is not required?
options: Vice Chairman of National Planning Commission
explain: While Constitutional body heads, Justices, and Ambassadors require parliamentary hearings (Article 292), the Vice Chair of the NPC is an executive appointment and does not.

q: 7. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, In cases where a female civil employee becomes pregnant, how many days of maternity leave is there?
explain: Following the latest amendments to align with labor laws, maternity leave has been extended to 98 days.

q: 8. According to the civil service rules, if the wife of a male civil servant gives birth, how many days of maternity care leave?
explain: A male civil servant is entitled to 15 days of maternity care (paternity) leave to look after his wife and newborn.

q: 9. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, how many days can an employee accumulate the vacation leave he/she has earned?
explain: Home leave can be accumulated up to a maximum of 180 days throughout the service period.

q: 10. According to Civil Service Act-2049, which of the following leave can get by Civil servants?
explain: Festival, Home, and Study leaves are all standard provisions defined within the Act and Rules.

q: 11. How many years of permanent service period should an employee has completed to get study leave?
explain: A civil servant must complete at least 3 years of permanent service to become eligible for study leave.

q: 12. Which of the following leave is not available to an employee of the Civil Service?
explain: 'Visit leave' is not a recognized category of leave under the Nepal Civil Service Rules.

q: 13. Who approves the extraordinary leave of a civil servant?
explain: Because extraordinary leave is for a long duration (up to 3 years or 5 total), it must be approved by the Government of Nepal (Council of Ministers).

q: 14. Which body recommends the appointment of the heads of constitutional bodies in Nepal?
explain: The Constitutional Council is the specialized body tasked with recommending names for heads and members of constitutional commissions to the President.

q: 15. When did the publication of Gazette begin in Nepal?
explain: The Nepal Gazette (Nepal Rajpatra) first began its official publication on Shrawan 22, 2008 B.S.

q: 16. How many parts were there in 'Nepal Gazette'?
explain: The Nepal Gazette is organized into 6 distinct parts, each categorizing different types of government notices, acts, and rules.
